issues.description: The ray-sphere interface is inconsistent: the header declares a function named check_sphere_hit(...) but the implementation defines ray_sphere_intersect(...) and the program calls ray_sphere_intersect(...). This name/ signature mismatch between header, implementation and callers will cause compile-time errors or undefined references and will block students from building or understanding the intended API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the function name and prototype consistent across header, implementation and callers. Either (A) change the declaration in example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.h to declare bool ray_sphere_intersect(const float*, const float*, const float*, const float); or (B) rename the implementation and all callers to check_sphere_hit(...). Ensure the header is included where the function is called so callers see the correct prototype.

issues.description: The template repository's header declares a function named check_sphere_hit but the corresponding implementation defines ray_sphere_intersect. The solution repository uses ray_sphere_intersect in its header. This mismatch (header vs. implementation in the template, and template vs. solution) creates a mapping/compilation confusion for students: they cannot reliably locate or call the intended sphere-intersection function and may be unsure which name to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the declaration in the template header to match the implementation and the solution: change check_sphere_hit(...) to ray_sphere_intersect(...), or vice versa rename the implementation to check_sphere_hit. Prefer aligning to ray_sphere_intersect in the template header to match the implementation and the solution.
